subject.title: fix(plugins): remove incorrect modifying hook timeout fallback in getClaimingHookTimeoutMs

question: Should a claiming hook with no explicit `timeoutMs` have an explicit bounded default, or is unbounded execution the intended plugin contract?
rationale: The patch removes the only current fallback while the public hook documentation describes omitted registration timeouts as using a runner default; source inspection cannot safely choose the intended availability and compatibility policy.

options.title: Define a claiming default
options.body: Keep a bounded, claiming-specific default and add runner-level regression coverage for omitted and explicit timeouts.

options.title: Make no timeout intentional
options.body: Accept unbounded claiming hooks only with explicit owner approval, documentation, and a runner-level test showing that behavior is safe.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Leave current behavior in place until the claiming-hook timeout policy is decided.

recommendation.title: Define a claiming default
recommendation.body: Keep a bounded, claiming-specific default and add runner-level regression coverage for omitted and explicit timeouts.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature-history trail ties this person most directly to the claiming-loop and hook-runner boundary.
